data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock futures are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures trade 2.7% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.8% and 1.15% respectively. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining around 4.5%.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, XTB research director Kathleen Brooks said.

"While technical indicators suggest that a recovery could be on the cards, the fundamental problems surrounding the AI trade remain," Brooks said. "The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered, for example, concerns about the profitability of the AI trade and financing costs."

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.95% in early trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 10% to $44.11 a troy ounce, while gold futures added close to 4% to trade around $3,680 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with benchmark Brent crude contracts gaining 1% to trade around $97.50 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts jumped 2.6% to trade around $85.90 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than seven basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a 25 basis point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Write to Joe Stonor at josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com

data.title: Tesla plans to acquire German manufacturing systems group EMAG
data.description:
Tesla has submitted plans to acquire German manufacturing systems supplier EMAG, which also makes parts for humanoid robots, a filing with Germany's antitrust authority showed on Friday.

Details on the planned transaction were not immediately known.

EMAG, headquartered near the southwestern city of Stuttgart, manufactures machines used to produce drive systems for humanoid robots.

data.title: CPTPP to start talks on accession of UAE, Indonesia, Philippines
data.description:
Members of the CPTPP Pacific Rim trade bloc have agreed to start accession negotiations with the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia and the Philippines, Vietnam's deputy trade minister said on Friday.

  • Members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership also agreed during a meeting in Hanoi to advance negotiations to upgrade the agreement, Luong Hoang Thai said, according to remarks shared by his office

  • Focus areas for an upgrade include services trade, e-commerce, customs and trade facilitation, cross-border services and business competitiveness, Thai said

  • The CPTPP is the successor to the Trans-Pacific Partnership, a bloc originally led by the United States that was widely seen as a counterweight to China's influence before US President Donald Trump withdrew Washington from the pact in 2017

  • It now comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, Vietnam and Britain

  • Deputy minister Thai said the CPTPP was confident in "reinforcing its leading role in promoting an open, stable, predictable and rules-based international trade and investment environment"

  • Its members also reaffirmed a determination to bring accession negotiations with Uruguay to an early conclusion

  • The scheduled two-day meeting took place hours after the Trump administration proposed tariffs on 14 of its trading partners – which included CPTPP members Japan, Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam – following its investigation into excess factory capacity

data.title: UBS Cites Experts that Rising Social Security Costs Pressure Intermediaries; Shenzhen Rent Uptick Supports Home Prices
data.description:
UBS recently held an expert call with senior management of a leading Shenzhen real estate intermediary and competitor of KE Holdings Inc . Experts believed rising social security contributions are having a negative cost impact on intermediaries. Some Shenzhen agencies are reportedly exploring replacing traditional employment contracts with freelance agent models to reduce the social security costs borne by intermediary firms.

For KE Holdings, experts foresaw Lianjia stores may need to absorb additional costs, while third-party store owners may bear higher costs and close less profitable outlets, or adopt freelance agent models similar to other intermediaries.

UBS cited expert estimates that overall residential rents in Shenzhen will rebound by about 3%, with rents in core and non-core areas rising about 3.5% and 2.5% respectively. The new Huanggang Port was expected to have a exceptionally positive impact on nearby properties, with residential rents hiking about 10% and home prices increasing a milder 2.5%.

Experts considered rising rents provide fundamental support for Shenzhen home prices to stabilize, as more investors focus on properties where monthly rental income can cover mortgage payments. UBS maintained its Buy rating and USD26.6 TP on KE Holdings.
